name: The Daylight Star Catcher
prompt: Set a broad black-lined funnel horizontally on a low rotating cradle. At its narrow end an astronomer projects a tiny patch of stars onto the inside of a white umbrella. Visitors queue in the brilliant sun to step under it.

name: The Puddle Ephemeris
prompt: Set out differently angled shallow pools of ink in a zigzag. Each reflects a different slice of sky. Observers move floating brass pins with long sticks to record a constellation as a broken diagram across the water.

name: A Constellation You Can Borrow
prompt: Stretch a large open embroidery frame between low stone posts. Astronomers stitch stars in yellow glass beads against gaps of clear sky. A removable triangular piece of the constellation travels on a handcart to the local school.

name: The Crater in the Courtyard
prompt: Make a huge matte-white relief of the lunar surface in a square sunken court. A mobile lamp on a curved red rail simulates the lunar day. Observers descend small staircases to mark shadow lengths beside individual craters.

name: The Telescope That Kneels
prompt: Articulate one long turquoise telescope into three segments on a low brass hinge. Its eyepiece bends to reach visitors of different heights while the upper tube stays aimed. A visible train of tiny adjustable mirrors carries the image around each elbow.
